Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           Minor plaintiff L.F. has initiated this case through his parent Sergey Firsov 1 against the

                                  14   Church of Scientology of Silicon Valley and Church of Scientology Mission of Silicon Valley

                                  15   (“Defendants”). Dkt. 1. Plaintiff has filed an application to proceed in forma pauperis (“IFP”).

                                  16   Dkt. 4. For the reasons stated below, the Court DENIES the IFP application with leave to amend.

                                  17   Accordingly, Plaintiff must file a renewed IFP application curing the deficiencies identified below,

                                  18   or else pay the filing fee in this action, no later than May 29, 2025.

                                  19           A district court may authorize a plaintiff to proceed in forma pauperis if the court is

                                  20   satisfied the would-be plaintiff cannot pay the filing fees required to pursue the lawsuit. See 28

                                  21   U.S.C. § (a)(1). “The right to proceed without prepayment of fees in a civil case is a privilege and

                                  22   not a right.” Elmer v. Comm’r of Soc. Sec., No. 22-cv-01045-SAB, 2022 WL 5237463, at *1

                                  23   (E.D. Cal. Sept. 21, 2022), report and recommendation adopted, No. 22-cv-1045-AWI-SAB, 2022

                                  24   WL 9452375 (E.D. Cal. Oct. 14, 2022) (citing Rowland v. California Men’s Colony, Unit II Men’s

                                  25   Advisory Council, 506 U.S. 194, 198 n.2 (1993)). “In order to proceed in court without

                                  26

                                  27   1
                                        The Complaint and application to proceed in forma pauperis style Mr. Firsov as Plaintiff’s
                                  28   “parent & guardian ad litem.” See Dkts. 1, 4. That distinction is irrelevant for the purposes of this
                                       Order and Plaintiff’s application.
                                         Case 5:25-cv-03265-SVK           Document 12         Filed 04/29/25     Page 2 of 2




                                   1   prepayment of the filing fee, a plaintiff must submit an affidavit demonstrating that he ‘is unable

                                   2   to pay such fees or give security therefor.’” Id. (quoting 28 U.S.C. § 1915(a)(1)). Here, minor

                                   3   Plaintiff L.F. has submitted such an affidavit through his parent Mr. Firsov. Dkt. 4. However,

                                   4   “where leave to proceed in forma pauperis is sought to vindicate the alleged substantive rights of a

                                   5   minor, the financial resources of both the minor and the volunteer parent, next friend, or guardian

                                   6   ad litem should be considered in determining ability to pay the costs of litigation.” Cottingham for

                                   7   Washington v. Bd. of Educ. of Emery Unified Sch. Dist., No. 93-cv-0824-DLJ, 1993 WL 79698, at

                                   8   *1 (N.D. Cal. Mar. 15, 1993) (cleaned up). Plaintiff’s application only contains information for

                                   9   L.F. himself and does not indicate Mr. Firsov’s resources as parent or guardian ad litem. This

                                  10   Court cannot evaluate Plaintiff’s ability to pay the filing fee without such information.

                                  11          Accordingly, the Court DENIES Plaintiff’s IFP application without prejudice to the

                                  12   Plaintiff filing a renewed IFP application by May 29, 2025. Such a renewed application shall: (a)
